approach: The study employed a multi-modal experimental design using C57BL/6 mice implanted with EL4 or RMA tumor cells. Key interventions included: 1) Administration of live F. prausnitzii (pre- or post-tumor challenge) combined with anti-PD-L1 mAb; 2) Direct supplementation with sodium butyrate to mimic bacterial metabolite effects; 3) Antibiotic pretreatment to induce dysbiosis, followed by F. prausnitzii rescue. Outcomes were assessed via tumor volume/weight measurements, droplet digital PCR and FISH for bacterial quantification, LC-MS/GC-MS for metabolomics (butyrate levels), flow cytometry and multiplex immunohistochemistry for immune cell profiling (CD8+, CD4+, PD-L1), Western blotting for pathway analysis (JAK-STAT/PD-L1), and 16S rRNA sequencing for gut microbiota composition changes. In vitro validation was performed on human NKTCL cell lines (KHYG-1, NKYS, YT).

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides mechanistic evidence that F. prausnitzii enhances anti-PD-L1 efficacy in NKTCL via butyrate-mediated suppression of PD-L1 and enhancement of CD8+ T cell immunity.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Findings are based on murine syngeneic models; clinical applicability to human NKTCL patients requires validation. The specific role of other metabolites besides butyrate remains unexplored.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Demonstrates that probiotic supplementation can counteract the adverse effects of antibiotic-induced dysbiosis on ICB therapy outcomes.
contribution_and_limits.limits: The study does not identify which specific 'beneficial' bacteria (other than F. prausnitzii itself) were restored or their individual contributions to the effect.

key_findings.conditions: Syngeneic NKTCL mouse models treated with anti-PD-L1 mAb + F. prausnitzii
key_findings.finding: Significant synergistic inhibition of tumor growth compared to anti-PD-L1 monotherapy, evidenced by reduced tumor weight and luminescence.

key_findings.conditions: Mice supplemented with sodium butyrate (16 mM) + anti-PD-L1 mAb
key_findings.finding: Butyrate recapitulated the synergistic tumor-suppressing effect of F. prausnitzii, indicating it is the key mediator.

key_findings.conditions: In vitro treatment of NKTCL cell lines with F. prausnitzii supernatant or butyrate
key_findings.finding: Downregulation of PD-L1 expression associated with inhibition of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.

key_findings.conditions: Tumor microenvironment analysis in combination therapy groups
key_findings.finding: Increased frequency of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and higher CD8+/CD4+ ratios; elevated IFN-γ levels; reduced PD-L1 expression.

key_findings.conditions: Antibiotic-pretreated mice receiving anti-PD-L1 mAb ± F. prausnitzii
key_findings.finding: Antibiotics compromised anti-PD-L1 efficacy; F. prausnitzii supplementation restored therapeutic efficacy and ameliorated antibiotic-induced gut dysbiosis (increased alpha diversity, restored beneficial taxa like Lactobacillus).

problem_or_question: To determine if and how F. prausnitzii can improve the suboptimal response rates of anti-PD-L1 therapy in NKTCL, and to elucidate the underlying immunological and metabolic mechanisms.
research_scope: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma (NKTCL) in syngeneic mouse models; gut microbiota modulation via probiotic supplementation and metabolite administration.
work_summary: This study investigates the potential of the next-generation probiotic Faecalibacterium prausnitzii to enhance the efficacy of anti-PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in NKTCL. Using syngeneic tumor-bearing mouse models, the authors demonstrated that F. prausnitzii supplementation synergistically inhibits tumor growth when combined with anti-PD-L1 antibodies. The mechanism was identified as butyrate-mediated downregulation of PD-L1 expression through inhibition of the JAK-STAT pathway, leading to enhanced infiltration of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells in the tumor microenvironment. Additionally, the study showed that F. prausnitzii could mitigate the negative impact of antibiotic-induced gut dysbiosis on ICB efficacy by restoring microbial diversity and composition.
